messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: node gpu-n53 reported CUDA OOM on runtime-service pod (cudaErrorMemoryAllocation) despite >10% headroom reserved. Automations flagged repeated OOMs across containers on that host.

chandra (oncall): ack. I'm jumping on it. Which tenants affected? any customer-facing 5xxs? :eyes:

sarah (support): saw elevated 500s from /v1/generate for customer:hedley-inc over the last 3m. Support ticket #7842 opened. Customer reporting timeouts.

ben (runtime): grabbing node telemetry now. Preliminary: allocator shows large number of small free blocks but reserved-block counter at ~92% used. Fragmentation metric (slab_frag_pct) spiked to 47%. KV cache reservations steady. Looks like pinned allocations preventing coalescing; OOM happens when a single large alloc fails.

alice (sre): can you paste the allocator dump? also check if prefetch/pinnable reservations triggered. Might be a reserve-pin race we saw before.

ben (runtime): logs + excerpt:
```
[2026-03-15T09:14:21Z] runtime: cudaMalloc failed: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
[2026-03-15T09:14:21Z] allocator: headroom=12.3%, reserved_blocks=92, free_blocks_small=312, free_blocks_large=2
[2026-03-15T09:14:21Z] runtime: attempt_shrink->evict_kvcache returned 0
```
No explicit pagefaults in dmesg; container OOM not triggered by kernel.

chandra (oncall): so headroom reported true but can't satisfy large contiguous allocation due to fragmentation. Is there recent model switch or rollout on that node?

ben (runtime): last deploy to that pool ~20m ago - quantized LLM variant rolled out. That variant increases max_seq and allocs larger temp buffers. Increased ephemeral allocations + pinned caches = fragmentation + reserved blocks pinned.

alice (sre): mitigation options (short-term):
- throttle incoming requests routed to gpu-n53 (set route weight 0.0 on router)
- drain pod and restart runtime container (fast)
- trigger soft-evict of KV cache for largest tenants on that node
- spin up spare node and move traffic (if autoscale can add immediate capacity)

chandra (oncall): prioritize minimal customer impact. Sarah: can we failover hedley-inc to other region/pool?

sarah (support): hedley-inc traffic is multi-region and sticky to US-west pool. We can fail to another pool but will need to update routing flag; ops can do quick fallback. Customer is on live experiment, impact medium.

ben (runtime): I can trigger a targeted KV eviction command: `curl -X POST http://runtime-admin/gpu-n53/evict?mode=largest` — that'll free some pinned blocks. Doing it now.

ops-bot: COMMAND: evict request submitted by ben (runtime). Job id=evict-2245009876-1.

ben (runtime): eviction returned ~4.6GB freed, slab_frag_pct dropped to 31%. But we still see a failing large alloc path for model attention cache (needs ~2.1GB contiguous).

alice (sre): good. Next: plan to restart the runtime pod to defragment allocations at OS/GPU level. chandra, want me to proceed?

chandra (oncall): yes proceed with a rolling restart of runtime container on gpu-n53. Mark as risk: short request loss for any in-flight requests. Notify support.

sarah (support): notifying hedley-inc: "We're performing a brief restart on a GPU host which may cause transient 5xxs; working to restore capacity. ETA 2-3m."

ops-bot: DEPLOY: restart runtime pod gpu-n53 initiated by alice (sre). kube rollout restart pod/runtime-abc-9f8d on node gpu-n53.

ben (runtime): after restart: allocator state: reserved_blocks=12%, free_blocks_large=5, slab_frag_pct=6%. Model allocs now succeed. No further CUDA OOM in the last 90s.

chandra (oncall): confirm customer impact resolved? Sarah?

sarah (support): hedley-inc reported requests recovering, 5xxs dropped to baseline. Close customer ticket when fully stable.

alice (sre): follow-ups:
- create postmortem to track root cause: reserve-pin + rollout increased large transient allocations.
- propose autoscaling tweak: warm spare nodes + faster bootstrap for heavy variants.
- runtime change: consider splitting large contiguous allocations or preallocating large slab pool to avoid fragmentation regressions.
- add telemetry alert: slab_frag_pct > 40% + reserved_blocks > 80% -> page to oncall earlier.

ben (runtime): filing PR with mitigation flag switch to disable aggressive prefetch for the quantized variant. Also adding diagnostic dump on evict failures.

chandra (oncall): happy path: recovered with eviction + restart. Escalation avoided. Assigning owner for follow-ups: alice (postmortem), ben (runtime fix), sarah (customer comms).

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2245, severity=high, owner=alice. Postmortem due in 72h.

alice (sre): oncall handoff: chandra, anything to add before I take ownership?

chandra (oncall): just log timeline and include the admin evict command in notes. No outstanding customer impact. Passing to alice for post-incident work. :white_check_mark:

alice (sre): taking over. I'll create the doc and schedule the blameless review. Closing this thread.
